# order: EO:1901  (WPA 1944: 1914 Mar 19)
# WPA summary: Violet Bacon Foster made eligiblefor reinstatement in the Civil Service Commission and transfer as clerk to the Foreign and Domestic Commerce Bureau without regard to the requirement of six months' servicepreceding transfer. 1914 CSR 124.
# book: Thirty-first Annual Report of the United States Civil Service Commission, fiscal year ended June 30, 1914
# scanned image 131, printed page 124; page lines 24-37
# source: https://archive.org/download/annualreport139commgoog/annualreport139commgoog_djvu.xml  sha256 748145327cc4747e27aefe00b5a3e31f5ebe8eb60b92a78e231aeb0237074ab1
# found by: date_and_subject; date 1914-03-19; words violet|bacon|foster|domestic
# Government printed copy (OCR of a compilation or report), not the signed original. A lead for the
# original_text step: read it against the scan before use. Exact slice of the page OCR follows.
----- EXACT SLICE -----
unsatisfactory conditions which prevail in the conduct of the farm at that penitentiary.
The Civil Service Commission is unable to concur in the recommendation for an
Executive order.
March 19, 1914.
The requirement of six months' service following reinstatement and preceding
transfer is hereby waived in the case of Miss Violet Bacon Foster, in view of the short
period during which she was separated from the service, and she may be transferred
to the position of clerk at $900 per annum in the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic
Commerce in the Department of Commerce.
Miss Foster was employed in the Civil Service Commission from July 1, 1903, until
September 20, 1913, on which date she was granted leave without pay on account of
ill nealth. On October 13, 1913, the leave was extended to November 1, 1913, when
she returned to duty.
March 23, 1914.
